panels.is: Theresa May in her BBC interview (shot 1 of 3): seated on a plain office chair, turned three-quarter to screen-left, looking at an interviewer off-frame left (never seen); dark wood-panelled backdrop; plum jacket, patterned blouse, grey hair. Framed about waist up and a little wider (Sam's framing, locked): her legs run off the bottom edge and the chair's base is out of frame by design. Flat cartoon house style, circle hands by design. Her line: 'The Prime Minister would do well to remember that we had a referendum, and in that referendum, the British public chose wolves.' Acting: composed, firm, reasonable; hands rest in her lap between gestures (a raised finger on 'well', an open palm on 'referendum', chops, open hands); she leans in on 'remember' and nods on 'referendum' and 'wolves'; a tight satisfied smile on 'wolves'. Mouths follow Sam's recorded voice (locked). This panel: Just after the line starts: both hands rest on her thighs.
